solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tofu regularly dunked in grim sauce for primates

indicators.note: the tofu letters are plunged into the middle of the sauce pieces

parts.note: dour means stern or grim
a coulis is a thin fruit or vegetable sauce

indicators.note: regularly takes letters at even intervals, here every other one

parts.note: only its second and fourth letters are used

explanation.surface: A recipe note: bean curd dipped in a gloomy-looking sauce, served to monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grim sauce' reads as one dish, but it is two pieces, an adjective and a noun, with the tofu letters dropped between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Douroucoulis are night monkeys of Central and South America, so they are primates.

clue.text: Enthralling custom, for the most part, not interesting old family member

indicators.note: only most of the word is wanted, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: dull means boring
O is the standard abbreviation for old
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A dull relative from the old days keeps up a fascinating family tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthralling' reads as 'fascinating', but it is meant literally as 'enslaving': DULOSIS is the practice of some ants of raiding other colonies for slaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthral originally meant to make someone a thrall or slave, and this habitual practice among certain ant species is exactly that kind of enslavement.

clue.text: Shady quality of boss, admitting fury over case of useless projection, in the main

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting over another comes before it
to admit is to let in, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: an umbo is the raised boss at the centre of a shield
rage is violent anger

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a ness is a headland jutting out into the sea

explanation.surface: A boss in a fury about some pointless sticking-out part at sea, and the shady character that goes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not an employer but the raised knob at the centre of a shield. 'In the main' means at sea, which is why the projection is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbrageous means giving shade, from Latin umbra for shadow, so the abstract noun names the property of being shady.

clue.text: Books a drive in Antipodean region

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
taken as written
drive in the sense of energy or vim, which is also go

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a road trip somewhere in Australia or New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests a car journey, but it is the noun meaning energy; 'Books' is not a verb for reserving but a collection of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region in the south of New Zealand's South Island, and New Zealand is part of the Antipodes as seen from Britain.

clue.text: Alchemist's work book supports one probing particle in electrolysis

indicators.note: something that probes pushes its way inside, so this pair enters the next word

parts.note: a cation is a positive ion drawn to the cathode during electrolysis

indicators.note: in a down clue a thing that supports another sits underneath it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A chemistry text describes a particle probed during the electrolysis an alchemist once performed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, book supporting one means the book letter sits below the one; that pair then probes the ion after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cibation, literally feeding, was one of the twelve processes of alchemy, in which the material in the vessel was replenished during the work.

clue.text: Launch bombs, wanting check for arm component

indicators.note: something that bombs is blown apart, so the remaining letters are scattered and rebuilt
wanting means lacking, so these letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An order to launch bombs is held back for lack of the right arming component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm component' sounds like part of a weapon, but it is the arm of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the human forearm, so it is literally part of an arm.

clue.text: Having equal rights, I really sense, must include terms from MeToo

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: taken as written
so, as in 'so good', means really or very
nous is common sense

indicators.note: terms are the ends or limits of something, so only the end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A campaigner insists that equal rights must take in the language of the MeToo movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' suggests vocabulary, as the surface wants, but it means the limits of the word, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Isonomy is equality of political rights before the law, from Greek isos equal and nomos law, and this is its adjective.

clue.text: Problem about school repeatedly including French in a paper for group of German learners

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: to include is to take inside, so one piece sits within the pair

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school, here used twice
en is the French word for in
taken as written
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A difficulty arises when a school keeps putting French into a paper aimed at German students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a placement word but belongs with 'French': the French for in. The Financial Times is London's pink business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: A Burschenschaft is a traditional German student fraternity, so it is a society of university pupils in Germany.

clue.text: Climber may put their foot in it, or arriviste ultimately — one sparing no effort

definitions.text: Climber may put their foot in it

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a trier is someone who always makes an effort

explanation.surface: A social climber, or an upstart, may blunder, but at least they try hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a social climber, which is why the arriviste fits the surface, but it is a mountaineer, and 'put their foot in it' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An etrier is a short rope ladder with a few rungs used in rock climbing, so a mountaineer literally steps into it.

clue.text: Dog knocking beetle off lips

indicators.note: to knock something off is to remove it, so these letters are struck out

parts.note: a Labrador is a breed of retriever
a dor is a kind of dung beetle

explanation.surface: A dog snaps a beetle off its lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' belongs with 'knocking' as the removal signal, not with 'lips'; the dor beetle is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Labra is the plural of labrum, the Latin anatomical term for a lip or lip-like part, as on an insect's mouth.

clue.text: Boarding boat in need of vacation, scrap transport arrangement in Chennai

indicators.note: to board a vessel is to go inside it, so these pieces are placed within
a vacated building is emptied, so the inside letters are cleared out and the shell kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
to scrap a decision is to undo it
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: Passengers boarding a boat in need of a break scrap the transport plans for Chennai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport arrangement' looks like one phrase, but 'transport' is BUS and 'arrangement in Chennai' is the definition; Chennai flags an Anglo-Indian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandobast, Anglo-Indian from Hindi and Persian, means organisation or a settled plan, so it is the Indian English word for arrangements.

clue.text: Don't go across river east of Berlin in noble estate

indicators.note: something stretched across another spans it on both sides, so it wraps around

parts.note: to stay is the opposite of to go
R is the abbreviation for river
Ost is the German for east

explanation.surface: A plea not to cross a river east of Berlin into some aristocrat's lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East of Berlin' reads as a direction, but it is the word for east in Berlin's language; STAY spans R and OST.
explanation.definitionFit: A starosty was a Polish crown estate granted for life to a nobleman, the starosta, so it is an aristocrat's landholding.

clue.text: Second piece of scale on some future fish dish

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after

parts.note: roe is fish eggs, which would become fish
S is the abbreviation for second
ti is a note in the sol-fa musical scale

explanation.surface: A second fish scale turns up on a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' points to fish scales, but it is the musical scale; 'future fish' is a witty way of saying eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a cake, so it is a named item of cooking.

clue.text: State ignoring a period of affluence and growth in Joburg

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out of account

parts.note: to state is to say or speak
taken as written
a boom is a time of economic prosperity

explanation.surface: A country left out of a time of wealth and development in Johannesburg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests economic growth, matching the boom, but it is a plant; Joburg, short for Johannesburg, flags a South African word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spekboom, Afrikaans for bacon tree, is a succulent shrub of South Africa, so it is a plant that grows there.

clue.text: Sole punishment ordered when pocketing cash, following overturned appeal

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command

indicators.note: one piece follows another, so it is written after it
turned over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A judge orders the only penalty, taking a cash fine, after an appeal is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' reads as only, but it is the sole of the foot; 'overturned appeal' sounds legal yet means SA turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastinado, also bastinade, is beating the soles of the feet with a stick, a punishment aimed squarely at that part of the body.

clue.text: Prevent leaks in Foreign Office? Briefly attempt to check ambassador

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so this piece wraps around the next
a brief version is cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: FO is the standard abbreviation
a try is an attempt
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A minister tries to stop leaks in the Foreign Office by reining in an ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaks' sounds like press leaks from a ministry, but they are leaks in a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: To fother is to stop a leak at sea by drawing a sail stuffed with oakum under a ship's hull over the hole.

clue.text: Cleaner accepting reason to walk? It's fruitful, but only once

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so this phrase goes inside

parts.note: a mop is a cleaning tool
having no car is a reason to go on foot

explanation.surface: A cleaner agrees to walk to work, a productive arrangement that happens just the once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitful' reads as productive, but it is literal: the plant bears fruit, then dies.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocarp is a plant that flowers and sets seed a single time in its life before dying, like an agave.

clue.text: Rebellious slave packs united, showing pluck

indicators.note: to pack something is to put it inside, so a letter is stowed within
rebellious things refuse to stay in line, so the letters break ranks

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A rebel slave rallies the others, a display of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' wants to be the noun meaning courage, which fits the rebel slave, but it is the verb meaning to pull off.
explanation.definitionFit: To avulse is to tear away or pull off forcibly, as in surgery or law, which is a violent sense of pluck.

clue.text: President manquée with head down in field

indicators.note: in a down clue the head is the top, so sending it down moves the first letter to the bottom

parts.note: Kamala Harris, who stood for US president in 2024 and lost

explanation.surface: A failed presidential candidate hangs her head out on the campaign field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manquée' is the feminine of manqué, meaning one who did not achieve what she aimed at, pointing to a woman who ran and lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrish is a dialect word for a stubble field left after harvest, so it names a kind of agricultural ground.

clue.text: Small antelopes mostly adore getting knocked over in legendary race

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the whole string runs backwards
most of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
gnus are wildebeest, a kind of antelope
to adore is to love

explanation.surface: Small antelopes, which love a run, get bowled over in a famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' suggests a running contest, but it is a lineage of people; 'mostly' trims only the adore word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volsungs are the heroic family of Norse saga, Sigurd's kin, so they are a race of people from legend.

clue.text: Swine loudly scoffed and whistled up north

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed is fed

explanation.surface: Pigs gobbled their food noisily and whistled in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' marks a Scots word; 'loudly' is the musical F for forte, not a sound clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowff is Scots for to whistle or hum softly, so its past tense is the northern dialect form of whistled.

clue.text: Are bosses in the oil industry displaying system for leasing land?

parts.note: people who run things are in charge
a rig is the drilling platform where oil is extracted

explanation.surface: A question whether oil executives show a way of renting out ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are bosses' is read as the verb run, with 'in the oil industry' standing for where oil workers are, out on a rig.
explanation.definitionFit: Runrig was the old Scottish and Irish arrangement of letting arable land in strips, rotated among the tenants of a farm.

clue.text: Arguments going back and forth about gutless ironic devil from Glasgow

indicators.note: the word is taken once backwards and once forwards
to be about something is to surround it, so the second copy wraps around

parts.note: a row is an argument, and two are needed

indicators.note: with the guts removed only the shell is left, so just the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Quarrels go back and forth over a spineless, sarcastic demon from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: One argument is needed twice, first read backwards and then forwards, with the second copy wrapped around the gutted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Worricow is a Scots word for a hobgoblin or the Devil himself, so Glasgow marks it as the Scottish name for a fiend.

clue.text: Rubbish bags for one upset figure synonymous with synonymy

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: rot means nonsense

indicators.note: in a down clue, set upside down means read from the bottom up

parts.note: e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A man whose name means synonyms is upset by a rubbish bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' reads as plastic sacks of rubbish, but it is the verb meaning captures.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous Thesaurus of English words and phrases, so his name stands for lists of synonyms.

clue.text: China, according to Indian, has area covered in sunshine towards the north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards
a thing covered in something is wrapped inside it

parts.note: a ray is a beam of sunshine
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An Indian traveller explains that northern China has a region bathed in sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country but rhyming slang: china plate means mate, so the answer is the Hindi word for friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaar is the Hindi and Urdu word for friend, used widely in Indian English, matching the British slang for a pal.

clue.text: Discover kind of skirt receiving top grade in local rating

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so this letter is put inside

parts.note: to suss is British slang for to work out
a ra-ra skirt is a short flounced skirt popular in the 1980s
A is the highest exam mark

explanation.surface: Someone finds a style of skirt earns top marks in a neighbourhood review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' sounds like a score, but it is the old sense of a scolding; 'local' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussarara is a Scots and dialect word for a severe scolding, and to rate someone once meant to berate them.

clue.text: Ancient scion of Teutonic noble with redoubled force

parts.note: Graf is the German title for a count
F stands for force, making a second F in the word

explanation.surface: The descendant of an old German nobleman fights back with double the strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scion' suggests a noble heir, matching the count, but it is a gardener's cutting; GRAF already has one F, so another doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Graff is an obsolete spelling of graft, and a scion is the shoot cut from one plant to be grafted onto another.

clue.text: Made crackling from old, engrossing recipe after cooking tons

indicators.note: to engross is to absorb wholly, so this word takes the rest inside it

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned

indicators.note: one piece comes after another, so it is written behind it
cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A cook made pork crackling from an old recipe, roasting tons of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackling' wants to be the crisp pork skin of the surface, but it is the verb, the sound of crackling.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrepitate is to crackle or burst apart when roasted, as salt crystals do, so it means made a crackling noise.
